validity.recommendation: Keep as its own segment, but confirm the 3-ProjectID split (P7460/P7466/P7467) of one named line is intentional; add OtherEnglishNames 'Akkas' (Okaz = Akkas transliteration); fill StartLocation = K3.
validity.researcher_notes: REAL, correctly classified planned pipeline. The sheet's own source (Jibawi / Iraqi Economists Network PDF, dated 2025-06, verified live with tokens 'K3'+'24') describes SCOP 'planning to construct a new dry gas pipeline from the Akkas gas field to Al-Anbar power station near Hit, Al Anbar Governorate' in THREE sections: (1) 26-inch Akkas field->T1, (2) 26-inch T1->K3, (3) 24-inch K3->Al-Anbar power station. Section (3) is exactly P7467 (segment 'K3 -Al-Anbar', dia=24). Its Table 1 lists the whole line as ONE project ('Akkas gas field - Anbar power station, 26 - 24, Dry gas') with NO length and NO capacity given. CLASSIFICATION: dry-gas transmission trunk feeding a power station = correct (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission both agree). DUPLICATE CHECK: not a double-count. P7460 (26" Akkas->T1) and P7466 (26" T1->K3) are the OTHER two physical sections of the SAME named line; all three GEM rows share the one gem.wiki page and the one single citation (the Jibawi PDF). P7467 is the distinct 24" K3->power-station section, so it is a legitimate separate segment rather than a relabel of another PID -- but three ProjectIDs for what the source treats as one project is worth confirming as intentional. NAME: 'Okaz' is a transliteration of 'Akkas' (Arabic عكاز/عكاس); every independent source uses 'Akkas'. Recommend OtherEnglishNames 'Akkas'. EXISTENCE / CORROBORATION caveat: the granular pipeline spec (3 sections, T1, K3, 24-inch) traces to a SINGLE origin -- SCOP's own Facebook announcement (Jibawi footnote 17, SCOP 2023-03-29), reproduced by the Jibawi review. No independent outlet describes the segmented pipeline or the K3->Anbar 24" section. What IS independently corroborated is the destination and rationale: the Anbar Combined Cycle Power Plant (~1,640 MW, under construction) is slated to be fed by Akkas dry gas -- confirmed by Wikipedia (Akkas gas field), OilPrice, and Iraq Oil Report (all verified live, tokens 'Akkas'+'Anbar'), plus Al Jazeera Arabic on the July 2025 Schlumberger field-development contract. So the pipeline is a genuine plan tied to a live project, but its specifics are single-source; tier medium.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status 'proposed' still correct. The Jibawi PDF (2025-06) describes the pipeline as SCOP 'planning to construct' -- no tender/construction start. Searched EN + AR for newer, dated evidence: the most recent independent reporting (attaqa.net, 2026-01-13; Iraq Business News/Al Jazeera on the 2025-07-22 Schlumberger field-development contract; Iraq Oil Report) confirms the Akkas field development is actively advancing (Phase 1 drilling underway, target 400 MMSCFD by 2027) and that its gas is destined for the Anbar power plant (~1,640 MW, under construction) -- but NONE reports that this feeder pipeline has been tendered or started construction. Did NOT apply the 2y-dormancy->shelved rule: although the pipeline announcement dates to 2023, the parent project (field + power plant it feeds) is demonstrably alive and progressing through 2025-2026, so the pipeline is not a dormant/abandoned plan -- it is contingent on a field ramp-up that is actively happening. Kept 'proposed'; most recent evidence 2026-01.

summary: P7467 real & correctly classified: the 24" K3->Al-Anbar power station section (3rd of 3) of the Akkas gas field->Anbar power plant dry-gas line; not a duplicate (P7460/P7466 are the other two sections); status stays proposed; caveats: pipeline spec is single-origin (SCOP), name should carry 'Akkas'; filled StartLocation=K3.
